mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority (National Police / Immigration Office of each individual's jurisdiction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country is party to the 1961 Apostille Convention) or Consular Legalization for non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate shareholder (if shareholder is a legal person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry or Ministry (Companies House, Registry of Commerce, CRS Authority)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry / Chamber of Commerce of shareholder's country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granted by each corporate shareholder to the proposed representative and/or Gérant for incorporation of the French SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or Company Registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All Ultimate Beneficial Owners, proposed Gérant (manager), and corporate directors must be screened prior to incorporation and refreshed every 90 days against: (1) Tracfin (French Financial Intelligence Unit) consolidated lists; (2) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (CFSP); (3) the UN Security Council Consolidated List (ISIL/Al-Qaida, Taliban, and related sanctions); (4) the OFAC SDN List and country-specific sectoral sanctions, particularly for USD-denominated Swift Wire transfers and any US-linked maritime escrow arrangements; and (5) public-domain PEP (Politically Exposed Persons) databases and adverse media. Any positive hit requires mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD), escalation to the designated AML compliance officer, and formal source-of-wealth assessment. For this Medium_Risk_Enhanced offshore marine charter scope, source-of-wealth evidence is mandatory for any UBO or PEP with direct or indirect shareholding ≥ 10%.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalities.entreprises.gouv.fr); name availability cross-checked via INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) and the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) through Infogreffe portals.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be expressed in a foreign language but must be transcribed in Latin alphabetical script. If the source language uses non-Latin script, a French transliteration must be filed. The name must include or be accompanied by the legal form designation 'SARL' (unless the full social name ordinance is used). The name must not be deceptive, must not infringe prior trademarks (French IP Code, Article L.711-2 et seq.), and must not be confusingly similar to existing registered company names at the RCS.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Établissement de crédit (requires prior authorization by ACPR)
Assurance / Insurance / Mutuelle (requires prior prudential approval)
France / République / État / National / Gouvernement (requires ministerial consent)
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross (protected by Geneva Conventions)
Offshore (not prohibited, but triggers enhanced AML/tax-substance review and requires clear commercial justification)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed company name by the Guichet Unique registry, the applicant may: (1) modify the name and resubmit via the same portal with a reasoned statement of distinctiveness; (2) file an administrative objection with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days of the refusal notification; (3) initiate a judicial challenge before the competent Tribunal de Commerce (or Tribunal judiciaire where commercial court absent) through an ex parte requête or référé procedure within one month of the refusal; and (4) where the refusal is based on public-order or trademark grounds, obtain a formal written opinion from INPI or a trademark attorney and reapply. Legal counsel may contest the refusal for arbitrary or erroneous application of protected-token rules. All appeal fees are governed by customary court tariffs.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual and domiciliation offices are expressly permitted in France under the domiciliation rules (Code de commerce, Article L.123-11 and R.123-11-2), provided the chosen provider is a professionally registered domiciliation company and maintains a physical French seat, local administrative management, and confidential handling of official correspondence. For the offshore marine charter industry, a pure virtual office without any local operational or administrative substance will be disregarded for tax substance purposes; however, for a holding/leasing vehicle without French crew or assets, a licensed third-party domiciliation office is generally accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% annual probability (Moderate-High) given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML classification and the targeted payment rails (Swift_Wire, Escrow_Maritime). Unannounced physical on-site inspections may be performed by the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and customs authorities to verify commercial substance, registered-office reality, and compliance with maritime chartering licensing conditions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L223-1 to L223-43 and R223-1 to R223-24 governing SARLs; Articles L123-1 to L123-9 governing registration; Articles L561-46 et seq. governing beneficial-owner declarations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE), administered through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) Guichet Unique, with registration in the competent Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained by the commercial court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of company formation submitted through the INPI Guichet Unique, supported by signed SARL articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration, and required supporting documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Contributions are deposited in a blocked bank or notarial account until registration. Capital contributions in kind require valuation by a commissaire aux apports unless the statutory exemption conditions are satisfied.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The sole shareholder or shareholders resolve that the subscribed share capital of the Company is hereby approved and that all cash contributions shall be deposited in the designated blocked account. The registered office is established at [full French address], effective upon registration. [Name] is appointed gérant for an indefinite term, with authority to represent and bind the Company within the limits of French law and the articles of association. The gérant is authorized to complete all registration, tax, banking, beneficial-owner, maritime, employment, and licensing formalities, and to execute any document required for commencement of the Company’s business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Name, Activities, and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique and the competent commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a compliant name, verify availability, define the corporate purpose to cover vessel ownership, chartering, leasing, maritime transport support, vessel management, and ancillary services, and secure a French registered office. Obtain landlord consent, domiciliation documentation, or premises title evidence.
required_dossiers: Registered-office lease, domiciliation agreement, or occupancy evidence
Identity and address evidence for each founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the corporate purpose, provide substitute address evidence, or respond to a registry request through the INPI portal before the stated deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private execution, with filing through the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language articles stating the name, form, registered office, purpose, duration, capital, share allocation, management, transfer restrictions, financial year, and dissolution rules. All founders sign the articles. Notarization is not generally required unless a notarial contribution, real-estate transfer, or special foreign-law document requires it.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate shareholder authority documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify missing signatures, inconsistent capital schedules, defective powers of attorney, or untranslated and unauthenticated foreign documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution, payment institution, or notary authorized to receive corporate capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account, transfer the required cash contributions, and obtain a certificate of deposit identifying the Company, subscribers, amount deposited, and account holder. The depositary may require enhanced due-diligence evidence for non-resident shareholders and source-of-funds documentation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the depositary's AML or KYC query, replace defective identification documents, or use a French notarial deposit account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Journal for Legal Notices (Journal d'annonces légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a formation notice in an authorized newspaper or approved online legal-notice medium in the department of the registered office. Ensure the notice states the company name, form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, gérant identity, and registration details required by applicable regulations.
required_dossiers: Articles or certified extracts where requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish a corrected notice and upload the new publication certificate if the registry identifies an omission or inconsistency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique for company formation and RNE registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic creation declaration, select SARL and the applicable NAF activity codes, upload the signed articles and supporting evidence, identify all beneficial owners, and pay applicable charges. Use certified translations and apostilles or legalization for foreign documents where required.
required_dossiers: Gérant identity, acceptance, and non-conviction declaration
Foreign shareholder corporate documents and powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI dashboard, cure queries within the assigned period, upload corrected documents, and resubmit without changing the filing reference unless instructed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court registry, INPI, INSEE, and French tax administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Kbis extract, RNE registration confirmation, SIREN and SIRET numbers, NAF code, and VAT identification where applicable. Release blocked capital after registration, activate the permanent bank account, and maintain statutory books and shareholder records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction through the INPI or registry portal, or file a formal rectification request with the competent commercial court registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Implement Corporate Governance and Compliance Controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company management; oversight by the competent commercial court registry and tax administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first management resolution, record the gérant appointment, establish signing authorities, maintain accounting records, schedule annual approval of accounts, and document related-party transactions. Register employees and implement payroll, social-security, AML, sanctions, anti-bribery, and beneficial-ownership controls appropriate to maritime chartering.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct governance records, approve missing resolutions, file late declarations where necessary, and seek professional advice for tax or employment regularization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Maritime Vessel Registration and Operating Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction générale des affaires maritimes, de la pêche et de l'aquaculture (DGAMPA), relevant maritime prefecture or DDTM maritime service, and French Customs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For each vessel operated or registered in France, complete ownership or lease documentation, vessel registration, safety certification, insurance, radio licensing, crew compliance, ISM/ISPS requirements where applicable, and the appropriate title of navigation. Determine whether the SARL acts as owner, armateur, technical manager, or bareboat charterer and allocate regulatory responsibilities contractually.
required_dossiers: Vessel title and ownership or lease agreement
Security plan and ISPS documentation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to maritime authority deficiencies, arrange class or flag-state corrective action, obtain temporary authorization where legally available, and appeal an adverse administrative decision under the French Administrative Justice Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction générale des affaires maritimes, de la pêche et de l'aquaculture (DGAMPA), supported by the relevant maritime prefecture, DDTM maritime service, French Customs, and port authority. France has no single generic industrial manufacturing licence for vessel leasing; maritime operation and vessel-specific approvals are mandatory.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: French vessel registration and applicable title of navigation (titre de navigation), together with vessel safety, security, radio, insurance, and maritime-employer approvals required for the vessel's flag, size, service, and operating area. A transport authorization or armateur registration may apply depending on the commercial operation and vessel status.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, through the competent regional environmental authority (Mission régionale d'autorité environnementale) and the relevant prefecture
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: The leasing of offshore supply vessels alone is generally not subject to a standalone full EIA. Port construction, dredging, shipyard, fuel-storage, waste-treatment, or shore-base projects require project-by-project screening and may require a full environmental impact assessment or authorization under the French Environmental Code. Classified installations may require ICPE declaration, registration, or authorization.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with MARPOL Annex I, IV, V, and VI; applicable IMO air-emission and sulfur requirements; EU port and waste rules; French water-police permits; and port reception procedures. Prohibit unauthorized discharge of oil, sewage, garbage, and hazardous substances. Shore facilities must comply with applicable ICPE emission, wastewater, hazardous-waste, spill-containment, monitoring, and recordkeeping limits. VOC controls apply where fuel or cargo-transfer operations fall within regulated activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain vessel and premises fire-safety compliance through approved inspections, maintain firefighting and lifesaving equipment, and satisfy the ISM and applicable SOLAS requirements. Shore offices, warehouses, workshops, and bases require building, occupancy, accessibility, and fire-safety compliance; establishments open to the public may require an ERP authorization. Conduct structural load and electrical inspections through competent or accredited bodies where required. Complete workplace risk assessment, occupational-health registration, seafarer medical fitness, training, personal-protective-equipment, emergency-plan, and labor-inspectorate compliance under the French Labour Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); central portal: impots.gouv.fr; French company registration portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL must first be registered with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, which issues the SIREN and SIRET identifiers. After RCS registration, the DGFiP automatically allocates the French Tax Identification Number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire). A foreign entity without a French establishment but carrying out taxable operations in France must apply to the DGFiP's non-resident tax department (Service des Impôts des Entreprises - non-résidents) using Form 1303-SD (demande d'attribution d'un numéro de TVA) together with supporting evidence of the taxable activity. For vessel chartering and maritime services, the entity must confirm its French VAT registration status before issuing invoices and may need a specific 'service en douane' code for customs and shipping formalities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a SARL is ipso facto subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) under Articles 206-1 and 209 of the CGI; it is not eligible for pass-through treatment. French-resident companies are taxed on worldwide profits, with a territorial adjustment for foreign-source profits attributable to a foreign establishment (Art. 209 I-A CGI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL cannot elect check-the-box pass-through taxation. Available elections include: (i) tax consolidation ('intégration fiscale') under Art. 223 A et seq. CGI for groups holding at least 95% of the subsidiary's shares; (ii) election for the 'régime mère-fille' (parent-subsidiary regime) under Art. 145 and 216 CGI; (iii) option under Art. 239 bis A CGI for civil-purpose SARLs — unavailable for maritime/commercial leasing activities; (iv) ATAD hybrid-mismatch declarations, where applicable, requiring Form 2257 to be filed with the DGFiP.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established SARL, VAT registration is compulsory from the first taxable transaction; there is no de minimis registration threshold. The 'franchise en base' small-business exemption applies only to domestic turnover until it exceeds EUR 85,000 for supply of goods and EUR 37,500 for supply of services (USD/EUR: EUR 10,000 annual EU-wide distance-selling threshold under the One-Stop-Shop). A foreign supplier to French B2B customers is caught by the reverse-charge mechanism and does not require French VAT registration unless it makes B2C supplies of services or distance sales above the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France will introduce mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting for all VAT-registered taxpayers under the 'réforme de la facturation électronique': from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises (including taxpayer groups), and from 1 September 2027 for small and medium-sized enterprises. Invoices must be issued in structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) through an approved Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF). Transaction data for all B2B and B2C supplies must be transmitted to the DGFiP in (near) real-time as e-reporting, including bank transaction detail. Although France does not operate a fully real-time fiscal clearance/stamping system, the DGFiP will automatically cross-check e-invoice and e-reporting data with VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically leaving EU territory are VAT-exempt under Art. 262-1-I CGI, provided the seller proves that the goods have left the EU within one month (or in justified cases, within a longer period). Additionally, under Art. 262-VI and 262-VII CGI, the sale, lease, and charter of commercial vessels used for operational activities on the high seas — including offshore platform supply vessels serving maritime installations — is VAT-exempt where the vessel is used for industrial or commercial purposes at sea and the charterer operates it outside territorial waters. The charter must be a marine charter with the vessel supplied, crewed, and operated for offshore logistics services; pure coastal or treacherous-navigation charters inside French territorial waters do not qualify. Zero-rating documentation must be retained for 10 years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/ENS) lodged via the DELTA-X electronic customs system showing the consignee and the 'export' authorisation
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill evidencing the high-seas destination and physical departure
Cargo manifest and Port Departure Certificate (certificat de départ) issued by the French customs authority at the departure port
Commercial invoice referencing the VAT clause 'EXONÉRATION ART. 262 CGI' and the nature of the marine charter
Bank document or fiche domiciliation export (for EUR remittance) proving inward receipt of the export consideration / Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate
Charter-party agreement and end-user certificate confirming offshore platform operations outside French territorial waters
Proof of arrival at the foreign or high-seas destination (e.g., offshore operations report, platform delivery note, or third-country customs entry)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the exporter fails to substantiate the export within 90 days after the expiry of the dispatch period under Art. 272(2) CGI, or fails to repatriate foreign-exchange proceeds within 180 days of shipment, the VAT exemption is retrospectively clawed back. The DGFiP re-assesses VAT on the full consideration, plus intérêts de retard (monthly late payment interest at 0.20% per month, accruing interest), under Articles 1727 and 1728 CGI. Penalties escalate based on intent: 40% for lack of good faith (insuffisance de bonne foi), 80% for abusive manoeuvres (manœuvres frauduleuses) or opposition to tax inspections; criminal penalties for customs false declarations under Art. 414 of the French Customs Code may also apply, including imprisonment of up to three years and fines. The DGFiP maintains a dedicated risk filter for maritime chartering and applies a presumption of missing export evidence if the vessel's GPS/port records do not match the declared itinerary.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as the central bank, with the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) under the Ministry of Economy and Finance exercising primary authority over foreign exchange regulations and capital controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. France, as a Eurozone member, adheres to EU free movement of capital provisions. Profit remittance is unrestricted, subject to standard anti-money laundering (AML) and tax reporting obligations. No prior authorization is required for cross-border transfers, but declarations are mandatory for transactions exceeding €10,000 or for any transfer to non-EU jurisdictions under the French Monetary and Financial Code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds is imposed. Exporters may retain foreign currency in designated accounts. However, all export receipts must be declared to the French customs and tax authorities for statistical and tax compliance. The reporting deadline is within 30 days of receipt, and the exporter must provide supporting documentation (e.g., commercial invoices, transport documents) to the bank for the transaction to be processed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Courant) and Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Fintech Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) licensed by the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) can provide cross-border payment services and multi-currency accounts. However, for high-value maritime charter transactions, traditional banks are preferred due to established correspondent banking networks and maritime trade expertise. EMIs may face limitations on escrow services and complex trade finance instruments (e.g., letters of credit). Legal constraints include the need for a full EMI license (not just payment institution) to hold client funds, and compliance with the EU's 5AMLD for beneficial ownership transparency.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the SARL's legal representative (gérant) is generally mandatory for initial account opening at tier-1 banks. Remote opening is permitted only for existing clients or via video-identification (e.g., using ACPR-approved digital KYC solutions) but is subject to enhanced due diligence, especially for non-resident directors. For offshore vessel leasing, banks may require an in-person interview at the branch or a notarized power of attorney if the director cannot appear. The interview covers business model, source of funds, and expected transaction volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value cross-border transactions with offshore counterparties (e.g., charter payments from tax havens)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Full charter party agreements with clear commercial terms; (2) Beneficial ownership declarations for all counterparties; (3) Invoices and bills of lading; (4) Vessel registration and insurance certificates; (5) Bank references from the counterparty's financial institution; (6) A detailed business plan explaining the operational necessity of the offshore structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership structure with multiple layers or non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (1) Corporate registry extracts (Kbis) for the SARL and all parent entities; (2) A clear organizational chart with ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) holding >25% equity; (3) Notarized copies of passports and proof of address for all UBOs; (4) Tax residency certificates; (5) A written explanation of the commercial purpose of the ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns (e.g., rapid in-and-out flows, large cash advances)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare: (1) A cash flow forecast and treasury policy; (2) Copies of all underlying contracts and invoices; (3) Board resolutions approving significant transactions; (4) Evidence of the vessel's operational schedule and charter hire receipts; (5) A letter from the external auditor confirming the legitimacy of the transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Use SWIFT MT103 for equity injections from shareholders. The purpose code must be '110' (Direct Investment) or '111' (Equity Capital) as per the French Balance of Payments classification. The bank will require a copy of the shareholder resolution, the capital increase deed, and the Kbis extract. For loans from non-resident shareholders, use purpose code '120' (Loans) and provide a loan agreement. All inbound transfers must be declared to the French Treasury via the 'Déclaration de Transfert de Fonds' if exceeding €15,000. Verification: The bank will perform a source-of-funds check and may request the underlying contract.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct payments to suppliers, charterers, or service providers; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for high-value vessel acquisitions or major equipment purchases, typically issued via the bank's trade finance desk; (3) Documentary collections (D/P, D/A) for lower-risk transactions. All outbound payments require a valid purpose code (e.g., '130' for services, '140' for goods) and supporting documentation (invoices, contracts). For payments to sanctioned jurisdictions, additional screening is mandatory.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts (FX Forwards) with maturities up to 12 months, available from tier-1 banks for EUR/USD and EUR/GBP pairs.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are not commonly used for EUR as it is freely convertible; however, they may be offered for exotic currency pairs (e.g., EUR/CNY) on a case-by-case basis.
Currency swaps (FX Swaps) for managing short-term liquidity mismatches between EUR and USD, particularly for charter payments in USD.
Options (FX Options) for hedging against adverse exchange rate movements, though these are less common for operational treasury and require board approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial accounts and management report (comptes annuels) filed in XML format
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year SARL due by 30 June following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: up to EUR 150 late fee plus additional per-month publicity charge and EUR 1,500 fine per director; persistent non-filing leads to administrative strike-off and potential director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, Cerfa 2065 and 2052/2059 schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar fiscal year: 3 May of following year; for non-calendar fiscal year: 3 months after closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: automatic 5% surcharge (10% after two months) plus 0.42% monthly interest; deliberate omission carries 100% penalty and may be subject to tax-liability assessment and criminal recovery.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CVAE (Cotisation sur la Valeur Ajoutée des Entreprises) annual value-added tax and headcount declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP / Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If taxable turnover exceeds EUR 500,000; due 3 May of the following year (calendar-year entity); if not taxable, no CVAE filing is due but declaration to the RCS should be updated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Misdeclaration or late CVAE return triggers automatic 5% surcharge, 0.42% monthly late interest, formal-notice penalty of 50%, and 100% penalty in case of bad faith.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CFE (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises) annual local business-property tax (franchise tax) payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Instalment on 15 June and final balance on 15 December per annual tax bill; no standalone return for unchanged structure, but changes must be declared within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment produces automatic 10% increase and monthly late charges plus enforcement actions; repeated failure may result in tax seizure and suspension of commercial activity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit required for SARL exceeding at least two of three thresholds: total assets EUR 4,000,000; pre-tax revenues EUR 8,000,000; average annual workforce 50. Parent companies controlling such entity may also require audit in the consolidated accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (ANC règlement 2014-03, Plan Comptable Général) is mandatory for statutory accounts; IFRS as adopted by EU is optional for unlisted SARL but mandatory for consolidated financial statements of public-interest groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO submission exists; beneficial-ownership information must be filed at incorporation and within 30 days of any transaction changing the ownership or control of the SARL. The annual accounts filing is cross-checked against the register of members, and all share transfers require annotation in the share register. False UBO statements are a criminal offense punishable by EUR 30,000 and 6 months imprisonment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / share transfer records
Register of Social Decisions / Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 330 – USD 1,650 for standard domiciliation; offshore ship-leasing business may require ship-charter agent office, typically USD 1,100 – USD 2,750 annually.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 12,000 for a single-vessel SARL mandatory audit; multi-vessel offshore fleets from USD 15,000 – USD 45,000.
